Subject: Helix - proposed Order Form redline and implementation window change

Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We discussed internally and would like to request a focused change order to the existing Order Form / Exhibit A: two main asks: (1) reduce the acceptance window in the Implementation Exhibit from 60 days to 45 days to align with our deployment plan, and (2) add an additional capacity tranche (10k token-hours) with a two-tiered price table for burst vs baseline usage.

I attached a redline of the Order Form (Helix_orderform_v3_redline.docx) with the proposed Exhibit table and a short matrix describing the acceptance milestone edits (implementation-acceptance-matrix.csv). High-level rationale: our integration timeline is compressed and we'd prefer a shorter acceptance window in exchange for a small implementation credit.

Can Redwood review the redline and confirm whether legal/finance can approve the price tiers and the 45-day acceptance? If the change is acceptable we can sign an amendment quickly.

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood: confirm legal acceptance and provide any required language edits + price impact note by Mon 8/17 EOD
- Helix: provide final signatory and send via DocuSign (I can originate)

Thanks,
Emily Rios

Helix Solutions

Emily —

Appreciate the clear summary and the redline. Quick acknowledgement: we received the docs and will route to Legal + Finance. Initial thoughts: the 45-day acceptance is operationally plausible but reduces our validation window; to mitigate risk we should (a) tie the acceptance milestone to the Exhibit acceptance criteria in the matrix and (b) include an automatic fallback to the previous 60-day window if a mutually agreed test harness isn't available within the first 10 days.

Laura, Karthik - can you and Legal take a look at the attached redline and the price table? Key asks for review:
- Confirm whether we can accept 45 days with the fallback language above
- Price: evaluate the burst vs baseline bands and propose a net effective rate (finance) and whether we should apply a one-time implementation credit if Helix accepts the 45-day term

Emily — I will come back with an internal decision and proposed language by end of day Mon 8/17. If there are contract edits we'll track them on the redline and respond inline.

Best,

Jonas / Karthik / Emily —

Quick legal + commercial notes after scanning the redline and price table. I attached a short price-impact workbook (price-impact-analysis.xlsx) with a back-of-envelope on the monthly run-rate delta. High-level items:

1) Acceptance window
- Legal is okay to move to 45 days provided we add explicit acceptance criteria bullets (we should reference the test harness in the matrix) and an automatic reversion provision: "If customer-provided test harness is not available by Day 10 from availability, acceptance window reverts to 60 days and both parties agree to an extended support runway." This protects engineering and avoids scope creep while being acceptable to customer.

2) Implementation credit
- Commercially, we can offer a one-time 8-12% implementation credit if Helix signs the amendment within 5 business days. Proposed default: 10% credit applied to the first invoice following amendment effective date. Finance signoff required.

3) Price tiers / capacity tranche
- Price bands look reasonable; Finance needs to confirm the effective blended rate for forecasting (I asked them to review the attached workbook). If they accept, we can fold the banded table into Exhibit A.

4) SOC2 / evidence ask
- We still need to ensure the SOC 2 evidence clause and log-retention appendix are properly referenced in the amendment. Emily — can you confirm your audit contact so Legal can align the DPA references?

Karthik — can you and Finance route the workbook to the billing manager and confirm whether the 10% credit is operationally acceptable? Also confirm whether we should pro-rate the new tranche for the current month.

If all good, I'll prepare an internal redline of the Helix doc and send back for counter-signature tracking.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: price-impact-analysis.xlsx
